candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 6 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR (per source-fidelity note). Ch 6 likely develops SUFFERING + PERSEVERANCE + FEAR-OF-GOD as the homiletic-catalog deepening the martyr-typology established by 1 Mq + 2 Mq's martyrdom-narratives. The everyday-Christian-as-confessor theme: martyrdom is not only physical-death-for-faith but also DAILY-PERSEVERANCE-IN-VIRTUE under temptation-and-distress. Parallels: 2 TIMOTHY 3:12 ('all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution'); 1 PETER 4:12-19 (the Petrine suffering-theology — 'beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you'); JAMES 1:2-4 ('count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations'); HEBREWS 12:1-13 (the cloud-of-witnesses + chastisement-as-fatherly-instruction). Tewahedo monastic-tradition preserves the martyr-typology-extended-to-everyday-life as the MARTUS-AS-DAILY-WITNESS framework.
